chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn Ahmad, from Yunus, who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman in one of the towns, so he asked her, 'Do you have a husband?' She said, 'No,' so he married her. Then a man came to him and said, 'She is my wife.' The woman denied that, saying it does not bind the husband. He (peace be upon him) said, 'She is his wife unless he produces evidence.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries a woman who claims she is single, but another man later claims she is his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in marital status, where a woman's declaration of being unmarried is accepted as valid until proven otherwise. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the burden of proof lies with the claimant of a prior existing marriage, ensuring stability in family law when evidence is absent. This ruling underscores the reliability of individual testimony in the absence of contradictory documentary proof, a key feature in classical fiqh debates regarding *zawaj al-mu'arrar* or simple contracts.
